method: camera traps at semi-arboreal (2-5 m) and terrestrial (40 cm) heights; activity pattern analysis of margay records
conditions: Wild margays in a privately protected area in Las Piedras, Madre de Dios, Peru (Hoja Nueva research station); camera traps at 62 sites over 80 nights in two grids (grid A July to September 2022, second grid September to November 2022). Results: the activity analysis is 'based on 64 records' with distinct nocturnal peaks at 12 am to 3 am and 5 am and 'notably at 6 pm' (Figure 5); the paper elsewhere reports 47 detections, 23 of them semi-arboreal, and the 64 and the 47 are not reconciled in the text read. The Discussion calls the activity 'predominantly nocturnal'; the paper does not report a percentage of records at night. Overlap with sympatric ocelot Dhat4 = 0.79 and with jaguarundi Dhat1 = 0.21 (other species, not filed). The text read mentions no bait, lure or attractant at the stations. The activity result pools the two grids and both camera heights.

source.authors: Zwicker S, Sánchez-Latorre C, Lukasser C
source.title: Increasing detections of the margay: occupancy, density, and activity patterns in Madre de Dios, Peru

quote: Activity pattern analyses indicated primary nocturnal behavior with peaks at midnight to 3 am, 5 am, and 6 pm.
